summary: The UK government says the Israeli authorities control entry to Palestine, including by sea to Gaza, and that you must show a passport and Israeli immigration slip to cross between Israel and Palestine. Canada's travel advice says travellers must pass through Israeli ports of entry and comply with Israeli entry requirements. Israel's Population and Immigration Authority says applications for B/2 tourist visas can be submitted at Israeli missions in the country of origin, and that under its eVisa-B2 pilot Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders residing in India and Sri Lanka can apply online. The UK says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024.

tips.text: The UK government says the Israeli authorities control entry to Palestine, including by sea to Gaza, and that you must show a passport and Israeli immigration slip to cross between Israel and Palestine.

The UK government says the Israeli authorities decide if you can enter Israel, that you may experience lengthy personal questioning and baggage searches when you enter and leave, and that entry stamps stating 'Palestinian Authority only' or 'Judea and Samaria only' have been issued to some travellers at the Allenby Bridge crossing with Jordan and at Tel Aviv Ben Gurion Airport.

The UK government advises against all travel to Gaza and says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024.

The UK government says travellers entering by the Allenby Bridge crossing must pass through Israeli checkpoints and Israeli-controlled territory to reach Jerusalem or Gaza, and to keep your entry card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it, particularly if you are crossing into Palestine.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Palestine?
faq.answer: The UK government says the Israeli authorities control entry to Palestine, and Canada's travel advice says travellers must pass through Israeli ports of entry and comply with Israeli entry requirements. Israel's Population and Immigration Authority says visitors from visa-exempt countries can apply for travel authorisation through the ETA-IL system, that applications for B/2 tourist visas can be submitted at Israeli missions in the country of origin, and that under its eVisa-B2 pilot Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders residing in India and Sri Lanka can apply online. For a visit to the Judea and Samaria Area only, COGAT says citizens of countries that maintain diplomatic relations with Israel but have no visa exemption agreement with it may apply to the Israeli representative office in their own country, at least 45 days before the date of entry.

faq.question: How do I get to the West Bank?
faq.answer: The UK government says the Israeli authorities control entry to Palestine and that you must show a passport and Israeli immigration slip to cross between Israel and Palestine. It says travellers entering by the Allenby Bridge crossing with Jordan must pass through Israeli checkpoints and Israeli-controlled territory to reach Jerusalem or Gaza.

faq.question: Can tourists visit Gaza?
faq.answer: No. The UK government advises against all travel to Gaza, says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024, and says consular support is not available from within Gaza.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Palestinian cities?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether, or where, Israeli citizens may enter the West Bank or Gaza.

faq.question: Will visiting the West Bank leave a stamp in my passport?
faq.answer: The UK government says visitors entering via Tel Aviv Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of an entry stamp in their passport, and that at other entry points you may get an entry card or a stamp. It says to keep your entry card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it, particularly if you are crossing into Palestine.
